digest.component_or_area: code-review gate impact model (v3 → v4 redesign)
propositions: Code-v3 impact model discards verifier-supplied prod_impact and trigger_likelihood for maint-lane findings, preventing test-sufficiency findings from reaching blocking threshold despite load-bearing guarded paths.

A test assertion forbidding a state that the same diff's contract declares allowed (contract-contradicting assertion) cannot be flagged as a serious defect in code-v3, as the tests binary lacks this antipattern and churn dampening caps priority at ~0.30 versus advisory threshold at 0.95.

Code-v4 re-scopes prod_impact and trigger_likelihood to rate user-reach of the guarded path (not diff file type), splits maint lane into serious/moderate/debt tiers with lane-scoped trigger maps and consequence-lane-only reversibility floor, and raises tests to blocking@0.54 to capture 99 changes (8.0%) versus v3's 42 (3.4%).

New binary forbids_contract_allowed_state in CodeSeverityAttrs emits when a test forbids a state the contract allows, with guard excluding deliberate stated tightening and pure-function exact-value asserts.

Code-v4 impact_code formula: serious binaries undamped (×1.0); moderate scaled by prod_impact multiplier and maint trigger map; debt scaled by churn amplifier only ([1.0, 1.5]); reversibility floor (0.6) applies only to consequence lanes with hard_to_reverse_surface, never to debt binaries.

Stored code-v3 sidecars remain unwritten (version-gated); v4 replay is offline analysis; absent binary contributes 0; test rewrites include deleted test_new_binary_scales_with_churn, re-targeted freq_mult tests to debt binaries, inverted reversibility floor case, and re-verified HIGH/NIT median separation >0.30 under v4.
